messages:
alex: seeing a p99 flare around 16:14 UTC on hosted-api, jumped from ~220ms to ~2.4s for ~6m. dashboard shows queue depth + kernel switchbacks. anyone on this?

maria: on it, pulling perf dashboards now. did we have any rollouts at that time?

sam: i can share a quick profiler dump in a sec. initial glance: a lot of short-sequence requests forced aux kernel exits and re-entry, heavy memcpy spikes.

ryan: tenant-fanout ratecap hit around the same window. looks like a small cohort sent many parallel short calls (chat/short) which increased coalescing pressure.

jin: KV cache metrics show eviction rate spiked ~3x and prefetch probe count doubled -> potential priming churn. could be noisy-tenant priming.

infra-bot: deploy-bot: rolled out api-serving v2.14.1 to hosted-prod at 16:10 UTC (canary -> 16:12 full). No rollbacks.

alex: ok deploy aligns. sam, paste the profiler snippet you mentioned.

sam: pasting top hot stacks (sampling profiler):

```
# samples
2000  runtime::kernel_select_aux()
1500  runtime::kvcache_prefetch()
1200  runtime::batch_coalescer::flush_path()
800   runtime::memcpy_async()
```

sam: note the kernel_select_aux hotspots correlate with short-seq traffic where we pick the aux kernel then fallback repeatedly. that causes cache invalidation patterns.

maria: dug into request logs for tenant cohort: many requests length ~40 tokens, high concurrency. batching heuristics are favoring tiny batches which increases kernel churn.

ryan: ratecap fanout meant requests were redistributed across more workers -> less effective KV cache locality. combined with tiny batches = thrash.

jin: here's kvcache evictions snippet from metrics query:
```
series: kv_evictions_total{pool=hosted-prod}
16:05 -> 120/s
16:12 -> 340/s
16:18 -> 110/s
```

jin: also saw prefetch probe failures: prefetch_misses went up. prefetch probes are allocating hot prefixes aggressively and then being evicted.

alex: hypothesis: deploy didn't change kernel behavior directly but traffic pattern + ratecap redistribution + batching config produced a pathological interaction: repeated aux kernel select + prefetch thrash -> p99 spike. agreed?

maria: agree. short-term mitigations: 1) temporarily tighten ratecap fanout for noisy tenant, 2) bump coalescer hold time to slightly increase batch window for short seqs, 3) disable prefetch probe for the tenant cohort.

ryan: i can apply ratecap tweak (low blast) now. will limit cross-worker fanout.

sam: i can push a safe config to increase coalescer hold by 5ms for short_seq class. low risk.

jin: i will add a targeted kv prefetch blacklist for that tenant. disable their probes for 30m.

infra-bot: config-bot: updated ratecap policy for tenant-id=tenant-42 (applied by ryan) at 16:36 UTC.

maria: applied coalescer hold +5ms to short_seq route at 16:38 UTC (sam).

infra-bot: config-bot: disabled kvcache-prefetch-probe for tenant-id=tenant-42 at 16:39 UTC (jin).

alex: metrics after mitigations: p99 dropped back to ~260ms within ~4m. queue depth normalized. eviction rate back to baseline. good.

sam: follow-ups: add telemetry to expose kernel_select flip frequency per-tenant; instrument batch size distribution per route; add an alert when kv_evictions/s spikes > 2x baseline for a 2m window.

jin: agree + add a prefetch_probe_hit_ratio metric and a per-tenant probe blacklist audit log.

maria: ops doc todo: run a runbook entry for this combo (ratecap fanout + short-seq batching + prefetch) and include recommended mitigations (ratecap, coalescer tuning, prefetch blacklist).

ryan: owns immediate postmortem blameless notes + timeline.

alex: tentative RCA: emergent interaction between (1) tenant burst causing ratecap redistribution, (2) short-sequence-heavy workload causing tiny batches and repeated aux kernel selection, and (3) aggressive kvcache prefetch probes producing eviction churn. Not a single code bug but a config/heuristic coupling.

maria: closing loop: will keep probes disabled for 1h, then re-evaluate under synthetic load. schedule perf experiment to replay tenant burst in staging with the new coalescer/selector metrics.

alex: thanks team. quick wins landed, follow-ups created: sam metrics, jin prefetch audit, maria runbook, ryan postmortem. will convert to incident doc. :thumbsup:
